Interface ImageProtocol

All Known Implementing Classes:
BrailleProtocol, HalfBlockProtocol, ITermProtocol, KittyProtocol, SixelProtocol
public interface ImageProtocol
Protocol for rendering images to a terminal.

Implementations may render images using character-based approximations (half-blocks, Braille patterns) or native terminal protocols (Sixel, Kitty, iTerm2).

  • Method Details

    • render

      void render(ImageData image, Rect area, Buffer buffer, OutputStream rawOutput) throws IOException
      Renders the image to the given terminal area.

      Character-based protocols write directly to the buffer. Native protocols write to the raw output stream.

      Parameters:
      image - the image data to render
      area - the terminal area (in character cells) to render into
      buffer - the buffer for character-based rendering
      rawOutput - the output stream for native protocol escape sequences (may be null)
      Throws:
      IOException - if writing to rawOutput fails

    • requiresRawOutput

      boolean requiresRawOutput()
      Returns true if this protocol requires raw byte output.

      Character-based protocols (half-block, braille) return false and use the buffer. Native protocols (Sixel, Kitty, iTerm2) return true and use rawOutput.

      Returns:
      true if raw output is required

    • handlesOwnScaling

      default boolean handlesOwnScaling()
      Returns true if this protocol handles its own pixel scaling via cell dimensions (e.g. Kitty's c=/r= or iTerm2's width=/height=).

      Protocols that return true receive the original full-resolution image and a display area computed in cells. Protocols that return false (Sixel, character-based) receive a pre-scaled image.

      Returns:
      true if the protocol handles scaling internally

    • resolution

      ImageProtocol.Resolution resolution()
      Returns the resolution multiplier for this protocol.

      This indicates how many "virtual pixels" each terminal cell can represent:

      • Half-block: 1x2 (1 column, 2 rows per cell)
      • Braille: 2x4 (2 columns, 4 rows per cell)
      • Native protocols: depends on cell pixel size
      Returns:
      the resolution multiplier
